name: Orca
description: Matrilineal cultural intelligence. Distinct pod ecotypes transmit unique hunting traditions — wave-washing seals off ice floes, beaching to catch sea lions, cooperative herring corralling — none of which are genetic. Knowledge passes from grandmother to mother to calf across decades. Post-reproductive females lead pods using accumulated ecological memory, the only non-human species with confirmed menopause tied to wisdom transmission.

core_attributes.neurology: matrilineal cultural memory, cooperative strategy learning
core_attributes.pattern: cultural hunting tradition, post-reproductive leadership, dialect transmission

scope.definition: Proportion of novel prey-capture techniques that spread from innovating orca to all members of the same pod within one breeding season, observed across North Pacific resident and transient populations.

evidence.source: Rendell & Whitehead (2001) 'Culture in whales and dolphins', Behavioral and Brain Sciences 24:309-324; Ford et al. (2000) 'Killer Whales', UBC Press — pod-specific hunting culture documentation.
cross_domain_examples: Norwegian carousel feeding: orca cooperatively herd herring with bubble curtains — technique spread within pod
Patagonia intentional stranding technique: transmitted from mother to offspring over 10+ years
Japanese macaque potato-washing: analogous cultural food processing technique spreading through social network

scope.falsifiability: If hunting innovations appear simultaneously in multiple pod members without observed interaction, independent invention rather than cultural transmission explains the pattern.
scope.measurement_limits: Transmission tracking requires multi-year longitudinal observation of identified individuals. Pod fission limits cross-pod transmission. Some techniques may be co-discovered rather than taught.

scope.definition: Correlation between pod hunting success rate and presence of oldest living female (matriarch, age 40+) — measured as hunt success change when matriarch is absent vs present over 10-year monitoring periods.

evidence.source: Brent et al. (2015) 'Ecological knowledge, leadership, and the evolution of menopause in killer whales', Current Biology 25:746-750; Foster et al. (2012) orca matriarch salmon knowledge study.
cross_domain_examples: pods with matriarchs age 50+ show 0.65 salmon hunt success vs 0.41 without matriarch in low-salmon years
matriarch knowledge of salmon run location 25 years prior correlates with current leadership accuracy
elephant matriarch herds: same pattern — older matriarch = higher survival in drought years (Moss 2001)

scope.falsifiability: If pods randomly led by any individual (not age-correlated) show equal hunting success to matriarch-led pods in low-resource years, accumulated knowledge is not the leadership advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Matriarch advantage is most pronounced in scarce-resource conditions. Abundant prey years show no significant difference. Tracking requires life-history records for individually identified whales over decades.

scope.definition: Proportion of pod-specific call variants (discrete calls) that remain consistent across 20 years of longitudinal acoustic recording, distinguishing pods acoustically from neighboring groups.

evidence.source: Ford (1991) 'Vocal traditions among resident killer whales in coastal waters of British Columbia', Canadian Journal of Zoology 69:1454-1483; Yurk et al. (2002) cultural transmission of calls.
cross_domain_examples: J-pod (Puget Sound) calls remain 92% consistent over 30-year recording period
call similarity tree matches genetic family tree — dialect is culturally inherited, not genetically encoded
human language dialects: analogous cultural transmission with geographic and social isolation as barriers

scope.falsifiability: If acoustic analysis shows orca calls are individually variable (not pod-consistent) over time, pod-level dialect as a distinct cultural inheritance unit is not supported.
scope.measurement_limits: Dialect stability requires multi-decade recordings of identified individuals. Pods that fission develop dialect drift within 5-10 years. Call complexity prevents automated classification — requires human expert validation.
